question: Which of the following is causative factor for oral cancer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tobacco**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tobacco use is the leading cause of oral cancer worldwide, accounting for approximately 90% of oral cancer cases.
 
• The harmful chemicals in tobacco, including nicotine and tar, can lead to mutations in the DNA of oral cells, causing cancerous growths.
 
• Both smoking (cigarettes, cigars, pipes) and smokeless tobacco (chewing tobacco, snuff) are significant risk factors for the development of oral cancer.
 
• Quitting tobacco use can significantly reduce the risk of developing oral cancer, highlighting the importance of tobacco cessation programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oral Cancer:**

 
 
• Oral cancer refers to cancer that develops in any part of the mouth, including the lips, gums, tongue, the inner lining of the cheeks, the roof of the mouth, and the floor of the mouth.
 
• Symptoms of oral cancer can include a sore in the mouth that doesn't heal, a lump, or a white or red patch on the gums, tongue, or lining of the mouth.
 
• Early detection of oral cancer can significantly improve the chances of successful treatment and survival.
 
 
 
• **Risk Factors for Oral Cancer:**
 
 
• Besides tobacco use, other risk factors for oral cancer include excessive alcohol consumption, human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, prolonged exposure to the sun (for lip cancer), and a diet low in fruits and vegetables.
 
• Genetic predisposition and a weakened immune system can also increase the risk of developing oral cancer.
 
 
 
• **Prevention and Early Detection:**
 
 
• Preventive measures include avoiding tobacco and excessive alcohol use, maintaining good oral hygiene, and eating a healthy diet rich in fruits and vegetables.
 
• Regular dental check-ups can help in the early detection of oral cancer. Dentists can spot early signs of cancer and pre-cancerous conditions in the mouth.
 
 
 
• **Treatment of Oral Cancer:**
 
 
• Treatment options for oral cancer include surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy, depending on the stage and location of the cancer.
 
• Rehabilitation and follow-up care are important aspects of the treatment process to ensure the best possible recovery and quality of life for patients.
